messages.content: I need to put together a Boston and New York work trip for June 22 through 26. I have an author dinner in Boston Monday at 6:30, a campus rights meeting all day Tuesday, then New York appointments Wednesday afternoon through Friday noon. I will leave from Denver, travel between the cities Wednesday morning, and fly home Friday.

I can compare the whole trip as one itinerary. Is the Boston dinner near Back Bay or Cambridge, and where are the New York appointments? Also, how much arrival margin would you like before Monday's dinner?

The dinner is in Back Bay and Tuesday's meeting is in Cambridge. In New York I need to be near the Flatiron District. I want enough time to check in and change before dinner, but I do not need most of Monday free.

Two Monday nonstops are worth comparing. A 7:05 a.m. departure from Denver reaches Boston at 12:50 p.m.; allowing about 30 minutes to deplane and 25 to 45 minutes to Back Bay, you should reach a hotel around 2:00. A 9:35 a.m. departure arrives at 3:20 p.m., which could put you at the hotel near 4:30 and leaves little protection against delay before the 6:30 dinner. The earlier flight is $318 and the later one is $267 in economy.
Use the earlier flight in the comparison. What does Wednesday look like by train? My first New York appointment is at 1:30 p.m.

From Back Bay station, the 7:15 a.m. Acela is scheduled into New York Penn Station at 10:58 a.m. The 8:10 a.m. Northeast Regional arrives at 12:05 p.m. The Acela gives you roughly two and a half hours before the appointment and costs $122; the Regional costs $71 but leaves only 85 minutes to exit Penn Station, leave luggage, and reach Flatiron. I would use the 7:15 train for this schedule.
Agreed. Please include the Acela. I will have one suitcase, so I need somewhere to leave it before the New York room is ready.

I will limit the New York hotel comparison to properties that have confirmed same-day luggage storage. For Boston, do you want to stay in Back Bay for the dinner and train, or Cambridge for Tuesday's meeting?
Compare both. I do not want an awkward trip to the station early Wednesday.

The Back Bay option is the Copley Square Hotel at $612 total for Monday and Tuesday nights. It is a short walk from the dinner and about 8 minutes by taxi or 12 minutes on foot to Back Bay station. Tuesday's ride to Cambridge would be about 20 to 35 minutes each way. The Cambridge option is Hotel 1868 at $548 total. It is convenient Tuesday, but Wednesday would require leaving around 6:20 for a taxi to Back Bay station, with a typical trip of 20 to 35 minutes and more exposure to traffic. The $64 savings does not materially improve the overall trip.
Keep Copley Square. Is there any reason to leave from South Station instead?

The same Acela originates at South Station at 7:10 a.m. Boarding there can offer a little more time to settle in, but you would need a 10 to 20 minute taxi from the hotel instead of the nearby Back Bay stop. Boarding at Back Bay at 7:15 is simpler, and your reserved seat remains the same. I would arrive at the station by 6:50.
That works. Now show me two New York hotels and Friday flights that do not force me to leave my last appointment early.

For Wednesday and Thursday nights, the Evelyn Hotel is $684 total and about a 7-minute walk from the Flatiron District. The Motto by Hilton Chelsea is $626 total and roughly a 12-minute walk. Both will hold your suitcase Wednesday before check-in and Friday after checkout. The Evelyn saves local travel time; Motto saves $58. For Friday, a 3:40 p.m. nonstop from LaGuardia arrives Denver at 5:55 p.m. and costs $294. A 5:25 p.m. nonstop arrives at 7:42 p.m. and costs $336.
My Friday appointment ends at noon near Madison Square Park. Can I realistically make the 3:40 flight after retrieving my bag?

Yes, but it is the tighter option. If you finish at noon, walk to the Evelyn, collect the bag, and leave by 12:25, a taxi to LaGuardia commonly takes 30 to 55 minutes at that hour. That should put you at the terminal around 1:00 to 1:20, more than two hours before departure. A major traffic delay would reduce the cushion. From Motto, retrieval adds about 10 minutes. The 5:25 flight gives ample margin but also creates a longer airport wait.
Use the Evelyn and the 3:40 flight. Please total that combination and compare it with the cheaper hotel choices.

The selected combination is $2,030: Denver-Boston flight $318, Acela $122, Boston hotel $612, New York hotel $684, and New York-Denver flight $294. Using Hotel 1868 in Cambridge and Motto in Chelsea would lower the booked travel total to $1,908, a savings of $122, but adds a more difficult Wednesday station transfer and extra walking or short rides around the New York appointments.
Add realistic local transportation so I can submit a complete estimate. Tuesday in Cambridge is at 9 a.m., and I expect to finish at 5.

Allow $150 for local transportation: about $45 from Boston Logan to Back Bay, $25 each way between Back Bay and Cambridge on Tuesday, and $55 from Flatiron to LaGuardia Friday. The hotel-to-Back Bay station trip can be walked, and Penn Station to the Evelyn is about a 20-minute walk; I have included a $10 contingency for a subway ride or short taxi. That brings the working trip estimate to $2,180. Meals and any hotel incidental holds are excluded.
I may not want to walk from Penn Station with the suitcase. Make that a taxi, and check whether the Monday arrival still leaves room for a flight delay.

Changing Penn Station to the Evelyn to a taxi raises the local transportation allowance by about $15, for a revised trip estimate of $2,195. On Monday, the scheduled hotel arrival is around 2:00 p.m. That leaves about four and a half hours before dinner. Even with a 90-minute flight delay and slower traffic, you would likely reach Back Bay around 3:45, leaving time to check in and change.
Good. Give me the complete itinerary and flag anything that still has to be verified before purchase.

Working itinerary: Monday, June 22, take the 7:05 a.m. Denver-Boston nonstop, arriving 12:50 p.m.; taxi to Copley Square Hotel and stay two nights. Attend the 6:30 p.m. Back Bay dinner, then travel to Cambridge for the 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. Tuesday meeting. Wednesday, walk to Back Bay station by 6:50 a.m. for the 7:15 Acela, arriving New York Penn at 10:58; take a taxi to the Evelyn Hotel, leave the suitcase, and stay two nights. After the Friday noon appointment, retrieve the bag and leave for LaGuardia by about 12:25 for the 3:40 p.m. nonstop to Denver, arriving 5:55 p.m. The estimated total is $2,195, including a $165 local transportation allowance. Before paying, verify flight numbers and operating carriers, current schedules, fare and bag terms, Acela seat assignment and change rules, both hotels' itemized totals and cancellation deadlines, Wednesday and Friday luggage storage, and whether either hotel adds a destination charge not included in the quoted total.
